what_it_does: To make AI models run faster and use less energy, engineers often replace the full-precision floating-point numbers inside the model with smaller, rounded integers (a process called quantization). There are two flavors: symmetric quantization, which centers the range around zero, and asymmetric quantization, which shifts the range to better fit lopsided data. Asymmetric fits real AI activation values better and hurts accuracy less, but it produces many non-zero values in a representation called bit-slices (think of slicing a number vertically by its binary digits), which kills the energy savings that come from skipping zero slices. Panacea introduces a method — adjusting where zero sits in the number encoding, and picking which bit-slices to use based on the data's own distribution — to push most of those non-zero slices back toward zero, then pairs this with hardware that skips zero slices entirely during the multiply-and-accumulate operations that dominate AI inference.
